name: Palazzo Ripetta
positioning: Family-owned hotel in a 17th-century convent in Rome's historic centre, minutes from Piazza del Popolo, with art, a secret garden and wellness suites
best_for: Travelers who want to explore Rome's historic centre on foot
Couples looking for a suite with a fireplace, a free-standing bath or a private sauna

facts.text: Palazzo Ripetta is a hotel within a 17th-century convent.
The Palazzo has been in the same family for generations.
The corridors were designed by the modernist architect Luigi Moretti and are lined with satin black doors.
The guestrooms rise up into the original convent ceilings, and tall windows overlook the secret garden and quiet side streets.
The hotel is minutes from Piazza del Popolo, and guests can walk from the door to the Pantheon and the Trevi Fountain.
The Tiber is just across the road from the hotel.
The lobby shows the owner's own contemporary art collection, including an original Warhol.
San Baylon is the hotel's gourmet restaurant, with cuisine by chef Christian Spalvieri.
Etere is the hotel's rooftop, with a Mediterranean vibe.
The concierge can arrange market visits, hands-on cooking sessions, wine excursions and seasonal truffle hunting.
The property holds a Green Key certificate for sustainability.

highlights.text: The 18th-century Salone Bernini was originally consecrated as the conservatory's church and has a ceiling fresco by Giacomo Triga.
A 3rd-century Roman sarcophagus has been turned into a fountain in the courtyard patio.
The Suite Wellness comes with either a sauna or a steam room in a mezzanine spa space.
The Charme Suite with Hydropool is a space designed for personalised wellbeing treatments.
Some Romantic Junior Suites have open fireplaces and others have free-standing baths.

considerations.text: In high season last-minute bookings for experiences can be difficult, so the concierge asks guests to let them plan ahead.
WhataHotel notes that the historic building puts constraints on room sizes.
